entry.title: Strategyproof Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Resource Allocation
entry.summary:
Online resource allocation faces two coupled challenges: (1) allocating scarce resources efficiently under uncertain future demand, and (2) ensuring that agents report task valuations and requirements truthfully (strategyproofness). Reinforcement Learning (RL) adapts allocation decisions through experience but does not necessarily ensure strategyproofness. Existing strategyproof RL uses a linear allocation rule, which limits the resource interactions it can represent.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents #ml-theory

entry.title: Neighborhood Deprivation Shapes Post-Flood Population Losses in Pune and Bandung
entry.summary:
Disaster research in high-income settings shows that better-resourced communities see population inflows and faster recovery, while disadvantaged communities suffer prolonged population loss. Whether this pattern holds in rapidly urbanizing cities of the Global South remains unclear. Here we show, using mobile phone data from Pune, India, and Bandung, Indonesia, how neighborhood-level changes in phone presence, a proxy for short-term population movement, relate to flooding and neighborhood deprivation.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE
entry.summary:
We describe the agent we submitted to the GLEE Competition, which plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion games against a shared pool of human and AI opponents. The agent is built around three central components: a classical game-theoretic solver to compute numeric moves, an online Bayesian layer to estimate opponent archetypes, and a language model to write accompanying messages. We utilize Rubinstein bargaining for bargaining, Faratin concession for negotiation, and Kamenica--Gentzkow disclosure for persuasion, and adapt those models to live opponents using two separate layers: a Bayesian estimate of the opponent's hidden discount factor, reservation value, or signaling reliability, and a Thompson sampling bandit over five moral-foundation framings coupled with an evidence-intuition spectrum to establish message register.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #llm #agents

entry.title: Beyond urban boundaries: Percolation reveals land-consumptive growth in India
entry.summary:
Cities often extend beyond their administrative boundaries, complicating assessments of urban sustainability. Using Global Human Settlement Layer data for India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975--2025), we develop a percolation-based framework for urban delineation. Within district-based regions, we apply unrestricted DBSCAN to spatial coordinates of 100-m cells with positive population and built-up surface.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Mapping Artistic Engagement with Quantum Technologies
entry.summary:
Quantum technologies (QT) are increasingly being taken up in artistic practices, for example in the form of visual artworks or quantum computer music. However, more comprehensive empirical studies on the temporal development and the different forms of QT-related art are still lacking. Therefore, this study conducted a systematic mapping and classification of QT-related artworks.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Superlinear cities, finite limits: Three characteristic scales of urban agglomeration
entry.summary:
Urban scaling research has established that many socioeconomic outputs increase superlinearly with city population, implying rising per-capita output. Although urban scaling models have incorporated infrastructural and dissipative costs, they have generally not identified the finite population scales implied by independently scaling benefits and diseconomies. We connect the classical urban-economic trade-off between agglomeration benefits and costs to a generalized scaling framework in which these quantities follow distinct power laws.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Conservative Policy Iteration For Zero-Sum POSGs. Occupancy-state reductions make dynamic programming possible for zero-sum partially observable stochastic games (zs-POSGs).
entry.summary:
Occupancy-state reductions make dynamic programming possible for zero-sum partially observable stochastic games (zs-POSGs). Existing point-based solvers usually optimise a central value function. This restores Bellman recursion, but it requires point-based updates over high-dimensional occupancy spaces.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #infosec

entry.title: When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure
entry.summary:
Token systems support repeated service exchange without monetary transfers, but their viability depends on the stability of token balances. We study token systems with compatibility constraints among agents. A requester is randomly sampled in each period, and only a few randomly sampled agents are available to provide service.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #probability-stats #agents

entry.title: Feedback autocratic strategies in stochastic games. A stochastic game is an optimal control problem for multiple agents in a stochastic environment.
entry.summary:
A stochastic game is an optimal control problem for multiple agents in a stochastic environment. Stochastic games contain important practical problems, related to environmental issues or traffic flows. If the number of environmental states is one, such stochastic games are called repeated games.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents
